chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'at ibn Muhammad, from Sama'at, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That a eunuch deceived a woman regarding his potency. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are separated, and the woman takes her dower from him, and his back is struck (with the cane) just as he deceived himself.'

key_terms.دَلَّسَ: To deceive or conceal a defect
key_terms.يُوجَعُ ظَهْرُهُ: His back is struck (with a cane for punishment)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a eunuch who maries a woman by deceiving her about his sexual capability?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *ikhtiyar* (choice) in marriage by detailing the compensation for a eunuch who concealed his impotence, a condition known as *ikhtilal*. The ruling ensures the woman's right to full dowry (*sadaq*) and imposes physical punishment (*jald*) on the husband as retributive justice for his deceit, reflecting the Shia emphasis on transparency in marital contracts. This case is frequently cited by jurists to discuss the validity of marriage when a specific defect is hidden from the spouse.
